articles.title: Luhay Hamido señala la puerta de salida a los que no crean en la salvación
articles.standfirst: Reunión a cuatro bandas en el seno del club y unanimidad para lograr la permanencia
articles.summary: Reunión a cuatro bandas en el seno del club y unanimidad para lograr la permanencia
articles.body: Tras un domingo agitado en el Alfonso Murube —con el presidente Luhay Hamido ofreciendo su dimisión y la directiva rechazándola por unanimidad para ratificarlo—, marcado por la derrota en casa ante el Sporting y la consolidación como colista en la categoría de plata, el Ceuta ha querido cortar de raíz el mal momento deportivo. Lo hizo a última hora de este domingo con una reunión de urgencia a cuatro bandas entre la propia junta directiva, la dirección deportiva con Edu Villegas al frente, el técnico José Juan Romero y toda la plantilla. El encuentro arrancó sin rodeos. Luhay tomó la palabra de inicio y puso sobre la mesa una propuesta drástica: cualquier futbolista que no se viera con fuerzas o compromiso para sacar esto adelante podía marcharse en ese mismo instante cobrando el cien por ciento de su contrato. Nadie quiso dar un paso al frente ni pidió salir. Al ver que todo el vestuario decidía quedarse, la reunión dio un giro: la puerta del despacho se cerró con llave. A partir de ahí, en un tono directo y sincero, el presidente preguntó cara a cara a los jugadores si de verdad estaban convencidos de revertir la situación. La puerta no se volvió a abrir hasta que cuerpo técnico, directiva y plantilla escenificaron un compromiso total. Todos a una afirmaron estar decididos a cambiar la dinámica y pelear por el objetivo marcado para esta temporada. En el club están convencidos de que este cara a cara a puerta cerrada debe marcar un antes y un después en el devenir del equipo. De momento, los números dicho que el equipo caballa solo ha sumado 5 puntos de 36 posibles, y que enfrente espera un mes de noviembre con un calendario realmente exigente. Habrá que ver si las palabras y el compromiso se traduce en una reacción sobre el terreno de juego.

articles.summary: Bet365 te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Borussia Dortmund y al Real Betis en el Signal Iduna Park, correspondiente a la cuarta jornada de la fase de liga de la Champions
articles.body: Borussia Dortmund y Real Betis se enfrentan en el Signal Iduna Park, partido correspondiente a la cuarta jornada de la fase de liga de la Champions League 2026/27. El duelo se juega este miércoles 4 de noviembre, a las 21:00. El conjunto de Manuel Pellegrini afronta el encuentro con el pleno de victorias: tres triunfos en tres partidos, con un 2-3 en Lille, un 3-2 al Porto y un 1-0 al Feyenoord, que le sitúan quinto con nueve puntos. El Dortmund, decimotercero con seis, suma dos victorias y una derrota, y llega con el recuerdo de su 3-2 al Villarreal en este mismo escenario. Favorito para el partido entre Dortmund y Betis Con todos estos datos, las casas de apuestas dan como favorito al Dortmund, aunque sin una diferencia demasiado amplia. Bet365 paga su victoria a cuota 1.70, un precio ajustado que refleja la fortaleza del conjunto alemán como local, donde ha ganado cinco de sus últimos seis partidos. Además, Guirassy atraviesa un momento excelente, con cuatro goles en tres partidos de Champions. El Betis, por su parte, no se presenta como un rival cómodo. Su victoria se paga a 4.33 en Bet365, una cuota que premia la sorpresa ante un equipo que no ha ganado por dos o más goles de diferencia en sus últimos ocho partidos. Los verdiblancos llegan sin conocer la derrota en Europa, con Bartra como protagonista inesperado, con dos goles en la competición. El empate, a cuota 4.33, completa un mercado en el que ningún resultado queda descartado, aunque algunos modelos de predicción apuntan precisamente a un 1-1. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan aparece como una de las alternativas más interesantes de las apuestas deportivas. El Betis ha marcado en los tres partidos de esta Champions, con una media de 2.3 goles por encuentro, y el Dortmund ha encajado en cuatro de sus últimos seis partidos. Es un equipo que, además, ha tenido problemas para mantener las ventajas, como se vio ante el Villarreal. Con estos datos, Bet365 paga el Sí a 1.53. Por otro lado, el conjunto alemán es muy fuerte en casa y llega con un delantero en estado de gracia. Si el Dortmund se adelanta pronto y obliga al Betis a abrirse, el No gana peso y cotiza a 2.38. Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta hacia un partido con presencia de tantos. En lo que va de Champions, los partidos del Dortmund acumulan una media de tres goles entre los que marca y los que recibe, y los del Betis suben hasta los 3.7. Ninguno de los dos equipos ha hecho un partido cerrado en esta fase, y la línea de 2.5 goles resulta asequible para el Over, que Bet365 paga a 1.53. No obstante, el Betis no ha ganado al descanso en ninguno de sus tres compromisos, con dos 0-0 en la primera parte, lo que habla de un equipo que se mide con cautela y que podría dejar el marcador por debajo de esa línea. El Under 2.5 se paga a 2.5. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de córners se presenta como una alternativa interesante para los apostantes. El Dortmund suele jugar con mucha presión en su estadio y busca amplitud por las bandas, lo que le lleva a acumular saques de esquina cuando el rival se repliega. El Betis, por su parte, ha mostrado un estilo de juego de transiciones rápidas, lo que suele traducirse en un volumen alto de saques de esquina por ambos lados. El Over 9.5 paga 1.8 en Bet365. Si el partido se decide pronto y el ritmo baja, el Under 9.5 podría ser una opción de valor. Su cuota es de 1.91.

articles.title: Se confirman las malas noticias con Gelabert
articles.standfirst: El mediapunta del Sporting sufre una lesión en el menisco interno de su rodilla y tendrá que frenar hasta 2027
articles.summary: El mediapunta del Sporting sufre una lesión en el menisco interno de su rodilla y tendrá que frenar hasta 2027
articles.body: No todo fueron alegrías para el Sporting durante el pasado fin de semana. El conjunto rojiblanco, que sumó una nueva victoria en el Alfonso Murube, emprendió el viaje hacia Ceuta con las alarmas encendidas por una posible lesión de rodilla de César Gelabert. Días después, y con tres puntos más en su casillero, se confirman las malas noticias en torno al ‘10’ del Sporting. Un mal gesto en la rodilla de Gelabert hizo saltar la preocupación en Mareo en el entrenamiento previo a viajar a Ceuta. Una acción que evitó que el palentino participase en la victoria del Sporting ante los de José Juan Romero. "Estuve en contacto con él, fue su cumpleaños. Ojalá esté disponible cuanto antes para los intereses de todos”, expresaba Nicolás Larcamón sobre la posible lesión del mediapunta. No se cumplirá el deseo del técnico del Sporting. La resonancia magnética a la que se sometió Gelabert en la mañana de este lunes confirmó una rotura parcial del menisco interno de su rodilla derecha. Una lesión que apunta a alejar al canterano del Real Madrid del césped durante los dos próximos meses de competición. El Sporting se queda sin César Gelabert hasta 2027.

articles.title: WSL: Lauren Hemp did not make the Ballon d'Or top 30 but her form for Manchester City this season deserves attention
articles.summary: Digital journalist Laura Hunter returns for a second season with a WSL-dedicated column, analysing all the big talking points from across the weekend's action; this week's focus is on the immense form of Lauren Hemp and why she can no longer be overlooked for the game's top accolades
articles.body:
Plenty of Manchester City's squad featured prominently in the women's Ballon d'Or final rankings last week. Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw rightly came third. Yui Hasegawa finished 11th, while Alex Greenwood and Kerstin Casparij were both named in the top 30. All such placings were a fair reflection of their current status.

But there was one glowing omission. Lauren Hemp, arguably the most in-form winger in the game right now, was curiously nowhere to be seen. It felt odd. And prompted a deeper dive into why she might have been overlooked.

Clearly Bunny Shaw is the undisputed champion of Man City's team, their top scorer and main driver of big results. Incidentally, the Jamaica international is currently on her best run of consecutive scoring starts in the league (8) and has found the net in 13 of 19 games in 2026. However, one might argue those numbers have been made more possible by the ingenuity of Hemp.

City's output is inextricably linked to the effectiveness of Hemp's connection with Shaw. She is her striker's main power source. Since the start of last season, Hemp has laid on six goals for Shaw, the most of any duo. Overall the pair have combined for a total of 20 goals, while Hemp assisting Shaw is the deadliest combination the division has ever seen.

This season Hemp has found Shaw with 12 crosses and they have linked for 14 chances. Those levels are unprecedented. "I've always said it's easy to play with Hempo," Shaw told Sky Sports at the weekend after beating London City Lionesses. "We've built chemistry for years now. When she's on the ball I know I have to make the run."

The sticking point in terms of recognition is therefore this: Hemp's personal goal return has been disappointing. She is the unselfish type and undoubtedly better at creating than scoring, a lesser-celebrated art form. Though a feeling exists within Manchester that Hemp is capable of changing such perception.

Nevertheless, her lack of goals is perhaps the biggest reason for her exclusion from the Ballon d'Or best grouping. Of course City were also not competing in Europe last year - although that did not hinder Shaw's appreciation.

While the headline numbers failed to reflect Hemp's immense role in City's domestic success last term, this year is different. Hemp is matching Shaw's ridiculous return pound for pound, the first pair of team-mates since Sam Kerr and Fran Kirby in 2021-22 to reach 10 goal involvements each in only eight games.

Their telepathic relationship underpinned Chelsea's most dominant era of success. Hemp and Shaw are similarly positioned.

"I can't find words on her," Andree Jeglertz said of his prize winger after her double in a 4-2 victory over Liverpool recently. "She just wants to play football. So I'm like 'how much structure and how much freedom do I give this kind of player?'

"I don't know what she is made of but she can run back and forward for the whole game. I'm so happy that she is scoring because that has been a little bit of a topic for her."

No doubt Hemp's scoring touch has returned. Whether buoyed by her new status as a WSL champion or just injury free and therefore fitter than in previous campaigns, her unlimited creative delivery has levelled up what Jeglertz's side are capable of in the final third.

City have recorded the most build up attacks (35) and most direct attacks (16) in the league this season, using Hemp's ability to mix attacking momentum from deep with her explosive running power and pace higher up the pitch. The difference in her positioning is discreet, as highlighted by the heat map below, but her instinct to crash the box is becoming more consistent.

While Hemp is averaging the same number of final-third touches per 90 as she was last season (34), her touches in the box have risen from seven per game to 10. Again the increase is subtle but highly impactful.

As such, she is getting on the end of chances herself as routinely as she is creating them for others. Her clever blind-side movement and deft finish won City the game at London City, where she shared the pitch with actual Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas - who wore custom made gold boots in a nod to her latest acclaim. The trophy was flaunted, too.

And yet, it was Hemp who shone brightest in Bromley, the creator of Shaw's opener from an unpredictable position centrally before scoring a brilliantly-timed winner. This is a player whose quality habitually decides games. And one who now deserves better recognition than the Ballon d'Or's most recent panel of judges were willing to give.

This weekend, the 26-year-old will equal Steph Houghton for the joint-most league appearances made for Manchester City. At such a young age that achievement is remarkable. She is already a WSL great. It's about time her broader reputation reflected as much.

articles.title: James Penrice: Upward path has Derek McInnes eager for Rangers deal
articles.summary: Rangers boss Derek McInnes stresses his desire to sign James Penrice on a permanent deal, with the full-back's impact leading to a first Scotland call.
articles.body:
It's been a very good few days for James Penrice, with a first Scotland call-up following on from a first senior semi-final victory, so it is little wonder manager Derek McInnes is so keen to keep him at Rangers.

The 27-year-old started like a train at Ibrox and has just kept going.

A day after signing on loan from AEK Athens, in his first outing of the season, the left-back turned in a player-of-the-match display, scoring and providing an assist in the 5-1 demolition of St Mirren.

It was Rangers' first win of the campaign after Europa League elimination and a tally of one point from their opening two games in the Scottish Premiership.

McInnes' side have not lost a domestic match since, stretching that run to 12 on Saturday as Penrice set up the only goal against Aberdeen at Hampden.

With his low shot turned home by Ryan Naderi, Rangers go into December's League Cup final against Hibernian looking for their first silverware since 2023. Penrice will hope to add to an unlikely medal set of Scottish League One and the Greek Super League.

AEK Athens paid £2m for the former Partick Thistle and Livingston defender in July 2025 after one stand-out year with Heart of Midlothian.

In Greece, he played 32 times for the side who secured their 14th national title. Sixteen of those appearances were starts as he alternated with Albania international Stavros Pilios.

The loan to Rangers includes an option to buy and reports from Athens suggest AEK would like to renegotiate given the impact Penrice has made.

Other reports have the fee agreed over the summer at a combined £1.2m, which looks like a steal.

"I've made my feelings clear on it," McInnes said. "Ideally, we'd like to have done it on a permanent, but the best way forward at the time was a loan.

"I think we are all aware of what it needs to be to make it permanent, but I think there is a lot of goodwill all round and that is something we would like to do."

McInnes on cup final carrot, Penrice future & Paisley trip

Is inexperience counting against youthful Rangers?

Penrice 'incredibly proud' of first Scotland call-up

McInnes sprang a surprise on Celtic by using Penrice in midfield for their League Cup meeting at Ibrox. The tactic worked a treat as Rangers romped to a 3-0 win.

He snuffed out the threat of Benjamin Nygren and moved wide in transition to great effect as the visitors were overwhelmed.

The same starting XI earned a 1-0 victory at Celtic Park a week later.

"What he's done since the first minute is just play with so much enthusiasm," McInnes said.

"He brings quality and energy. The fans take to him because of how he performs and how much he wants to win.

"He's a player that I trust and the supporters trust, so hopefully we can make it a longer-term thing."

A relatively late bloomer, Penrice spoke of his pride and a "weird feeling" to RangersTV after being named in the Scotland squad for this month's Nations League double-header against North Macedonia and Switzerland.

"I didn't ever think going through the early part of my career, I would ever be called up," he said.

McInnes shared his delight in the recognition while stressing it comes as "no real surprise" given current form. Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli echoed those thoughts, describing the selection as "logical".

Scotland skipper Andy Robertson will overtake Sir Kenny Dalglish's record of 102 caps if he plays in both games, so an uncapped left-back might have to be patient.

Then we have Kieran Tierney on 58 caps and Josh Doig embarking on his fourth Serie A campaign, so competition in that area is stiff.

"James deserves it and hopefully he can get on the pitch and come back with a couple of caps," McInnes added.

"The thing that screams out of James is hunger. He's driven himself to get to where he is now. He plays with hunger and he trains with hunger.

"I don't think anybody should ever underestimate working with hungry players.

"As soon as you become too comfortable, you become complacent, for me. And I think that there is a real hunger there to establish himself here. He wants to be here."

articles.title: Enrique Riquelme da la bienvenida a Nadal al Madrid y le pide ayuda para “evitar la venta del club”
articles.standfirst: El que fuera rival de Florentino Pérez en las elecciones de junio aprovecha la entrada del tenista en la directiva para trasladarle las reivindicaciones de su plataforma de socios
articles.summary: El que fuera rival de Florentino Pérez en las elecciones de junio aprovecha la entrada del tenista en la directiva para trasladarle las reivindicaciones de su plataforma de socios
articles.body: Enrique Riquelme, quien fuera rival de Florentino Pérez en las elecciones a la presidencia del Real Madrid del pasado junio, ha reaccionado a la propuesta del club de que Rafa Nadal se incorpore a la Junta Directiva con un mensaje público en el que mezcla la felicitación y las reivindicaciones que defiende su plataforma de socios. “Querido Rafa, es una alegría tener a alguien como tú en el Real Madrid. Íntegro, leal y gran madridista”, arranca el texto, en el que Riquelme apela a una afinidad personal con el tenista: “Contigo el Madrid gana y, como hemos comentado en varias ocasiones, siempre, Primero el Madrid”. A partir de ahí, el empresario traslada a Nadal su agenda. “Seguro que tú nos ayudas a evitar la venta del club, dignificar ser socio del Real Madrid y evitar las irregularidades que viven miles de socios, logrando más transparencia y democracia”, escribe, antes de invitarle a conocer de primera mano su plataforma: “Con ganas de invitarte a que conozcas las inquietudes y los problemas de los socios”. El mensaje se cierra con una petición directa al balear: “Ahora tú puedes hacer mucho por los socios desde dentro. Confiamos en ti. Gran abrazo, amigo. ¡Hala Madrid!”. La bienvenida llega el mismo día en que la directiva anunció la propuesta de que Nadal se incorpore nuevo miembro de la Junta, un nombramiento que deberá ratificar la Asamblea General de Socios Compromisarios el próximo 21 de noviembre. La referencia a “evitar la venta del club” alude al plan de reordenación societaria que maneja el Real Madrid para abrir la puerta a capital privado, una de las cuestiones que Riquelme situó en el centro de su campaña electoral frente a Florentino Pérez, que revalidó la presidencia con el 65% de los votos. El guiño a la cercanía entre ambos no es casual. Riquelme y Nadal mantienen una buena relación nacida en el terreno de los negocios y el deporte: el Grupo Cox, la empresa del alicantino, es el patrocinador principal del Team Rafa, el equipo con el que el tenista compite en el mundial de lanchas eléctricas, y se les ha visto juntos en actos como la premiere de la docuserie del manacorí. Esa amistad, de hecho, llevó a vincular al extenista con la candidatura de Riquelme en primavera, un extremo que el propio Nadal desmintió: “Aunque tengo una buena relación con Enrique, tengo un grandísimo respeto por Florentino”.

articles.title: Jesus de Miguel: Goalkeeper Jesus Owono experiencing 'most difficult days of my life' after Tenerife forward's death following collision
articles.summary: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel died after a collision with FC Andorra's goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who has now released a statement; Lautaro Spatz also took to Instagram to defend his team-mate, who has deleted his account on the social media platform
articles.body:
The Tenerife forward died on Tuesday morning following a collision with Owono during a Spanish second division match on Monday.

Owono was sent off for the clash having raced from his goal and struck 30-year-old De Miguel at force, with the Tenerife player subsequently suffering a cardiac arrest after being taken into intensive care.

"These are the most difficult days of my life," ‌Owono said in a statement. "I struggle to find the words, and I find it very hard to ​process what has happened. I know there will be many questions to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.

"But right now, honestly, ​I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the ⁠pain we are experiencing. Rest in ⁠peace, Jesus."

Owono deactivated his Instagram account on Tuesday after receiving abuse online.

Andorra said that they were offering psychological support to anyone at the club who needed it following De Miguel's death.

Andorra centre-back Lautaro Spatz defended his team-mate ‌Owono on Tuesday evening.

"I also want to say a few words about my team-mate, goalkeeper and friend, who is deeply affected by what has happened," Spatz said on social media.

"Those of us who know him know the kind of person he ⁠is, how much he is suffering at this moment, and ​that he would never intentionally hurt anyone."

"In football, unfortunate ​incidents can happen, but no one could imagine that one of ​them might end with such tragic consequences," continued Spatz, also sending his ⁠condolences to De Miguel's family and Tenerife.

The Equatoguinean Football Federation expressed support for Owono in a statement on Tuesday, adding that the 25-year-old was going through a situation of ⁠profound sorrow and grief.

Owono has made 47 ​international appearances for Equatorial Guinea.

Meanwhile, Can Vidalet goalkeeper Michel Owono said on social ​media that he was receiving racist abuse, with people confusing him with the Andorra player.

Spanish national police have opened a ‌routine investigation into De Miguel's ​death.

Fans gathered at Tenerife's Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium to lay tributes to De Miguel, with the club declaring six days of official mourning.

A memorial service will be held at the ground on Saturday evening for the striker, with supporters invited to attend.

Tuesday's domestic Spanish games were called off as a mark of respect but Champions League matches went ahead, including Barcelona's clash with Aston Villa at the Nou Camp.

A minute's silence was held ahead of the contest, which Barca won 3-0, with Raphinha scoring twice.

Speaking to CBS Sports afterwards, the Brazilian refused to talk about the game, saying: "I want to send a lot of strength to the family of Jesus. Today I'm not going to talk about football.

"For me, the truth is it was quite difficult (to play). After seeing the news, of course I didn't have good feelings. He's a fellow player and it could have happened to anyone, it could have happened to me.

"He was the same age as me, I don't know if that's why it affected me more. It's been a difficult day. Personally, it touched me a lot."

Arsenal also held a minute's silence at their training session to remember De Miguel, while manager Mikel Arteta addressed the situation in his press conference.

"Absolutely heartbreaking," said Arteta. "Watching back the action, the incident, what happened, to see a colleague lose his life in such a manner, it's beyond any words that I can put today.

"So, on behalf of everybody at the club, we want to send our condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, all his loved ones, and to Tenerife as well because it's been a really difficult day."

The Tenerife match was suspended after the incident, which occurred in stoppage time, with distressed players calling for immediate medical attention.

A statement from Tenerife announcing De Miguel's death read: "We stand alongside his devastated family, alongside his loved ones… that today weep for this cruel outcome."

In their own statement on Tuesday evening, Andorra said the club were "deeply shocked", adding: "The first thing we want to do is express our most sincere condolences to his family, CD Tenerife and all those who were close to him.

"We know that no words can ease such pain, but we want them to know that we are by their side and that we deeply share their sadness."

articles.title: Hearts record £2.4m loss in Bloom's first year
articles.summary: Heart of Midlothian record a loss of £2.4m for the year ending 30 June, despite a turnover of more than £23m the first 12 months of Brighton owner Tony Bloom's involvement.
articles.body:
Heart of Midlothian have announced a loss of £2.4m for the year ending 30 June - the first 12 months of Brighton & Hove Albion owner Tony Bloom's involvement with the Scottish Premiership club.

The accounts show turnover was more than £23m, which is a club record sum for a season not involving European competition, as they missed out on their first Scottish title for 66 years following a final-day defeat by reigning champions Celtic.

Bloom invested £10m to take a 29% non-voting stake in Hearts, who were looking to benefit from his Jamestown Analytics recruitment network.

Hearts, who will hold their annual meeting in early December, indicate an amount of £1.8m was gained on player trading during the period, with £7.8m spent on acquisitions.

In a statement to shareholders, Hearts say they expect a significant improvement in the next set of accounts due to "further momentum" in player trading.

Did Vrancken get key decisions wrong in Hampden defeat?

Thun prepare for Hearts with four-goal fightback to win

Hearts point out that "like-for-like revenue [was] up 20%" during a season but say the loss for the year was because they "took a deliberate decision to invest in the playing squad from a position of financial strength, helping secure a return to European league phase football".

"With European income returning and further progress in player trading, the club anticipates a significantly improved financial result in 2026/27," they state on their club website.

Hearts point out that sponsorship and advertising income was up 37% and retail and hospitality income by 17% while continuing to "benefit from exceptional financial backing from its benefactors and Foundation of Hearts members", the latter contributing £1.49m alone.

As for Bloom's investment, the club points out that, while it improved their financial position and ability to improve the squad, "as an equity investment, this funding is reflected in the balance sheet rather than recognised as income in the profit and loss account".

Their "player trading gains" were 30% up on the previous year and "further gains will be reflected in the 2026/27 financial year following player trading activity completed in July and August".

Hearts claim their "balance sheet remains robust, with the accounts reporting net assets of £20.3m at the 30 June 2026 financial year-end".

They add that they are "engaged in positive discussions regarding further investment" to assist with their long-term ambitions.

articles.summary: Tenerife striker De Miguel died on Tuesday as a result of injuries from a collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Owono.
articles.body:
FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono said he is enduring the “hardest days of my life” after the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel , whom he collided with during a Spanish second division match on Monday.

The 30-year-old Spanish footballer died on Tuesday as a result of injuries he suffered in the collision with Equatorial Guinea international Owono , who had raced into midfield to clear an aerial ball.

“These are the hardest days of my life. I struggle to find the words, and it is very difficult for me to process anything that has happened,” said Owono in a statement published by his club Andorra on Wednesday.

“I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, of his family, and of all the people who loved him.

“I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are going through. Rest in peace, Jesus.”

Spanish police sources told the AFP news agency that an investigation into what happened has been opened, under judicial supervision.

Andorra players observed a minute’s silence on Wednesday before a voluntary training session, which Owono, 25, did not attend.

Owono received support from the president of the African country’s federation, Venancio Tomas Ndong Micha, in a letter of condolence following De Miguel’s death.

“I feel compelled to convey all our solidarity and support at this time to our player Jesus Lazaro Owono,” Micha wrote.

“We know that, as the involuntary protagonist of this tragic incident in the game, he is living through this situation with deep sorrow and distress.

“From the Equatorial Guinea Football Federation, we offer him all our human and professional backing, fully aware of the harshness of this event, which no one in our sport ever wishes to witness.”

Andorra defender Lautaro Spatz posted on Instagram in support of Owono, whom he said was “deeply affected” by what had happened.

“Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone,” wrote Spatz.

“In football, unfortunate incidents can happen, but no one could imagine that one of them might end with such tragic consequences.”

Earlier on Wednesday, it was confirmed that Tenerife and Andorra’s Spanish second division matches scheduled for the weekend would be postponed.

Tenerife were due to face Granada away from home, while Andorra were set to welcome Mallorca.

“After the tragic news of the death of Tenerife player Jesus de Miguel, the game … this Saturday November 7, at Nuevo Los Carmenes [stadium], has been postponed,” said Granada in a statement.

Mallorca said, “At times like this, respect and sensitivity in the face of a situation of profound grief must come first.”

The Spanish football federation postponed all Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina matches this week as a mark of respect following De Miguel’s death.

Tenerife plan to hold a tribute to De Miguel at the club’s stadium on Saturday, which supporters can attend, and are holding a six-day mourning period.

The club said the first team, board and staff will attend De Miguel’s funeral, which will take place in Navahermosa, in the province of Toledo on the Spanish mainland, where he has family roots.

A minute of silence was held before Champions League matches on Tuesday in honour of the striker, with the same planned for the rest of the week’s fixtures, organised by European football’s governing body UEFA.

articles.title: Aranbarri se queda sin laterales izquierdos
articles.standfirst: Bernat e Imanol sufren sendas roturas musculares
articles.summary: Bernat e Imanol sufren dos roturas musculares. Arbilla se perfila como su sustituto
articles.body: Los contratiempos se acumulan en el lateral izquierdo. Imanol García de Albéniz y Juan Bernat han caído prácticamente a la vez y serán baja durante las próximas semanas. Dos roturas musculares que les obligan a parar y a buscar alternativas para el carril zurdo de la zaga. El lateral vizcaíno sufre una rotura en el sóleo de la pierna derecha, mientras que el jugador valenciano presenta una rotura en el isquiotibial derecho. En el caso de Bernat, la lesión supone un frenazo en seco después de haber dejado atrás los diferentes problemas físicos que le acompañaron en los últimos años. El ex del PSG había sido titular en 10 de las 12 jornadas, aunque no terminaba de alcanzar su mejor versión. Diferente situación la de Imanol, que sufrió un esguince de tobillo en pretemporada y no pudo entrar en una convocatoria hasta la sexta jornada. Desde entonces, sólo había disputado 95 minutos repartidos en los dos últimos partidos. Será la evolución de sus respectivas recuperaciones la que marque el regreso a los terrenos de juego, pero, a corto plazo, Aranbarri deberá buscar soluciones. El elegido será Anaitz Arbilla. El capitán ya actuó como lateral el pasado sábado ante el Almería tras la lesión de Bernat y todo apunta a que repetirá en esa posición durante las próximas semanas. Rindió a un gran nivel como lateral la pasada temporada y ahora volverá a cambiar el eje de la zaga por la banda. Aranbarri también cuenta con otras alternativas, como cambiar de perfil a Álvaro Rodríguez y Cubero, además de disponer de la opción del canterano Ortuzar. Sin Bernat ni Imanol y con Arbilla como lateral, el técnico armero deberá buscar también otra pareja de baile para el eje de la defensa. Peru Nolaskoain y Elgezabal parten con ventaja, pero mientras el 4 no esté recuperado de su lesión, Arana y Jair pugnarán por un puesto al lado del jugador de Zumaia.

articles.title: El Rennes le niega la décima a Imanol
articles.standfirst: Su Olympiacos empató a domicilió y puso fin a una racha de nueve victorias consecutivas
articles.summary: Su Olympiacos empató a domicilió y puso fin a una racha de nueve victorias consecutivas
articles.body: Imanol Alguacil entró con el pie izquierdo a Olympiacos tras estrenarse con derrota frente al OFI Creta. Desde entonces, habían logrado encadenar una racha de nueve victorias consecutivas... que se ha victo frenada en su visita al Rennes (0-0) en la cuarta jornada de la Europa League. Era la segunda visita de Olympiacos a territorio francés tras imponerse al Marsella en el Vélodrome... y saltó al césped con una personalidad que sorprendió al Rennes. Con Gustavo Puerta y Gustavo Sá al mando de las operaciones, trató de ser protagonista, instalarse en campo rival y tantear a Brice Samba. El primer remate, cargando el área por parte de la 'Hormiga' González, llegó antes de cumplirse el primer minuto de partido. Leon Bailey, en el 19', probó con un disparo raso desde el 'piquito' del área y, acto seguido, Gustavo Puerta buscó la escuadra con un 'latigazo' desde larga distancia. Fue mediada la primera parte cuando el Rennes comenzó a hacer pie en el partido. Sobre todo, apoyándose en el balón parado. Rouault cabeceó una falta lateral por encima del larguero y, de inmediato, Stefan Ortega le sacó una mano abajo a Cresswell a la salida de un córner. Apretó el Rennes, en especial Al Tamari, antes de poner dirección al túnel de vestuarios. Tuvo que tirar de reflejos Stefan Ortega para repeler un 'cañonazo' a cargo de jordano desde el lateral del área al primer palo. Al filo del descanso, eso sí, el linier invalidó un gol en propia de Onyemaechi por fuera de juego del propio Al Tamari. Hizo bastante daño Nagida, una de las últimas sensaciones surgidas desde la prolífera academia del Rennes, e Imanol reaccionó dando entrada a Pedersen por Saliakas en el lateral derecho. Además, Olympiacos también intentó desplomar las revoluciones con las que finalizó la primera parte volviendo a agarrar el balón. El Rennes, por su parte, siguió empujando. La intención pasaba por robar alto, combinar en pocos toques y finalizar jugadas. Con el transcurso de la segunda parte, ambos equipos comenzaron a abrazar la posibilidad de dar por buenas las tablas. Sólo Al Tamari seguía haciendo la guerra por su cuenta... pero no logró romper la igualdad en el marcador.

articles.title: Jay Rodriguez: Ex-Burnley striker and England international announces retirement
articles.summary: Former Burnley striker Jay Rodriguez announces his retirement from playing career.
articles.body:
Former Burnley striker Jay Rodriguez has announced his retirement.

The 37-year-old England international began his career with the Clarets and eventually left his hometown club to join Southampton in 2012.

He made one England appearance in 2013 and subsequently joined West Bromwich Albion before returning to Turf Moor in 2019.

He won promotion to the Premier League twice with Burnley and finished his career with Wrexham, helping them win promotion from League One in 2025.

Rodriguez played more than 250 Premier League games during his career and in total made 311 appearances for Burnley across his two spells with the club.

His solitary England appearance came in a friendly against Chile at Wembley, during his spell playing for Southampton.

Rodriguez also helped the Saints to the EFL Cup final in 2016-17, in which they were defeated by Manchester United.

Rodriguez appeared 25 times for Wrexham and had been without a club since leaving the Welsh side in the summer.

articles.title: Uno a uno del Real Madrid contra el AEK: Valverde corona otra epopeya
articles.standfirst: Analizamos la actuación de los jugadores y de José Mourinho
articles.summary: Analizamos la actuación de los jugadores y de José Mourinho
articles.body: El Real Madrid encontró en Atenas, cuna de las grandes epopeyas, una resurrección con aire de déjà vu. A una hora poco habitual para él —las 18:45 h—, el conjunto de Mourinho remontó un 2-1 adverso para ganar por 2-3 al AEK y seguir firme en Europa, y lo hizo repitiendo al pie de la letra la receta de Roma: los mismos cambios que ya le funcionaron en el Olímpico —Endrick, Espí y compañía desde el banquillo—, la misma decisión de retirar a un Vinicius que no remonta el vuelo, y un desenlace de epopeya. El empate de Mbappé reavivó a los blancos y, en el descuento, un cañonazo de Valverde con la derecha firmó una victoria al más puro ADN madridista. Primera parte: Apareció con una acción tempranera para desbaratar con el pie una ocasión de Gacinovic. Nada pudo hacer en el gol de Koita. Minutos después sacó otro disparo potente de Jovic. Nota al descanso: 7 Segunda parte: El segundo gol del AEK se le coló entre las piernas. En líneas generales, no tuvo demasiada actividad. Nota final: 6 Primera parte: Intentó profundizar por banda derecha y pisó área en varias ocasiones. Le puso un buen pase a Vinicius en boca de gol, pero el brasileño partió en fuera de juego. Nota al descanso: 7 Segunda parte: El segundo gol griego transcurrió por su banda. Puso un gran centro raso a Mbappé, que esperaba en el área chica para embocar el 2-2. Nota final: 7,5 Primera parte: Fue su primera titularidad tras superar su larga lesión. Los minutos iniciales no dieron tregua al brasileño. Con el Madrid dueño del partido, no sufrió apenas. Nota al descanso: 5,5 Segunda parte: Probó desde lejos con un disparo potente que sacó el portero del AEK. No llegó a tapar el centro del 2-1, aunque lo lógico es que fuese tarea de Dumfries. Nota final: 5 Primera parte: Caso parecido a Militao. Jovic volvió locos a ambos centrales durante el primer tramo de la primera parte. Nota al descanso: 5,5 Segunda parte: No tuvo apenas implicación en el gol del AEK, aunque se espera que la defensa del Madrid sea más sólida ante rivales así. Nota final: 5 Primera parte: Koita le dejó clavado con un movimiento en la acción del gol. Asistió a Bellingham con un pase desde la izquierda en el 1-1. Nota al descanso: 6,5 Segunda parte: Rozó el gol en una jugada que remató en el segundo palo, pero un defensa despejó su disparo prácticamente bajo palos. Vio la amarilla en el 65'. Se marchó en el 81' por Carreras. Nota final: 6,5 Primera parte: No llegó a cortar el inicio de la jugada del 1-0 del AEK en el mediocampo. Tuvo bastante influencia en el juego del Madrid cerca del balcón del área con el equipo griego atrincherado en su campo. Nota al descanso: 6 Segunda parte: Salió del campo en el 67' por Valverde. Nota final: 6 Primera parte: Su déficit no estuvo en el despliegue, sino en ganar duelos. Apareció como coche escoba en algunas ocasiones del AEK. Nota al descanso: 5,5 Segunda parte: Se le vio algo más cómodo y certero en los duelos. También en las labores de recuperación. Nota final: 6 Primera parte: Se movió a la derecha con la presencia de Vinicius. Lo hizo bastante bien para dejar solo a Mbappé en la frontal. No tuvo tanto protagonismo en los uno contra uno como solemos verle cuando está por izquierda. Nota al descanso: 5 Segunda parte: Pese a no exhibirse tan bien como en izquierda, el trabajo es innegociable para el costamarfileño. Buenas ayudas en defensa. Salió del campo en el 67' por Endrick. Nota final: 5,5 Primera parte: Hizo su gol, pero el inglés estaba en fuera de juego. Con el siguiente no ocurrió lo mismo. Un pase de Cucurella desde la izquierda lo remató Jude de tacón. Golazo del inglés para empatar el encuentro. En términos de juego, casi todo pasó por él. Nota al descanso: 8,5 Segunda parte: Bajó un poco las revoluciones en la segunda parte. Vio muy bien a Dumfries en la jugada del 2-2. Se marchó en el 85' por Carreras. Nota final: 8 Primera parte: Comenzó intentando varios uno contra uno... pero no logró superar a su rival en ninguno. Intentó remontar con un disparo que tocó un defensa y atrapó el meta. No le salieron las cosas, aunque estuvo más participativo que en otras ocasiones. Nota al descanso: 5 Segunda parte: El gol del AEK viene de una jugada en la que el brasileño no llega a controlar el balón tras pase de Mbappé. No remonta el vuelo. Se marchó en el 81' por Brahim. Nota final: 4 Primera parte: Tuvo la primera del Madrid con un disparo que se marchó muy alto. Estaba bastante liberado el galo. Buscó situarse fuera del área para recibir y tener más protagonismo. Nota al descanso: 6 Segunda parte: Realizó una gran maniobra en una jugada que casi supone el 1-2 para el Madrid. Probó con un gran disparo al palo largo que estuvo cerca de colarse por la escuadra. Volvió a intentarlo poco después con un disparo algo templado. Estuvo donde tenía que estar un '9' para anotar el 2-2 a pase de Dumfries. Rozó el tercero de los blancos en un contragolpe, pero se topó con el larguero. Nota final: 7 Segunda parte: Entró en el 67' por Bernardo Silva. Qué barbaridad de latigazo soltó en el descuento. Un cañonazo con pierna derecha que dio al Madrid los tres puntos en Atenas. Imparable para el meta del AEK. Nota final: 9 Segunda parte: Entró en el 67' por Diomande. Le puso un gran pase al espacio a Mbappé que casi significa el 2-3. Dio algo de electricidad al Madrid, algo que necesitaba. Nota final: 8 Segunda parte: Entró en el 81' por Cucurella. Se sumó al ataque en varias incorporaciones. Nota final: s/c Segunda parte: Entró en el 81' por Vinicius. Puso algún balón al área en busca de la cabeza de Espí y los centrales. Nota final: s/c Segunda parte: Entró en el 85' por Bellingham. Nota final: s/c Primera parte: Su equipo sufrió demasiado durante el primer tramo de partido. Mejoró y logró atrincherar al AEK en su campo. Pudo haberse ido con ventaja al descanso. Nota al descanso: 5,5 Segunda parte: Al Madrid le costó más encontrar la portería al inicio del segundo tiempo. Estuvo cerca del gol en varias ocasiones, pero sufrió el revés del segundo del AEK. Repitió la fórmula de Roma y los cambios cambiaron algo la cara al equipo. Endrick sumó y Valverde coronó con un latigazo. Nota final: 7

articles.title: How landmark Everton compensation prevented Burnley record loss
articles.summary: Burnley have published promising financial results, but under the hood is a payment from Everton which makes the picture look far less positive.
articles.body:
Six years ago, Burnley were considered one of the best-run clubs in the country.

The Clarets were debt free, with £41.65m cash in the bank, and enjoying their fifth successive season of Premier League football.

Now they sit in the Championship relegation zone, with concerns over debt and the way the Clarets were bought by ALK Capital using loans and the club's own money.

Fans have been very concerned about what the future holds - although on Wednesday there was some rare positive news in the club's accounts.

BBC Sport takes a closer look at what is going on at Turf Moor.

You may be familiar with the term "leverage buyout" after the Glazer family's purchase of Manchester United in 2005.

It effectively means that a purchase is carried out using debt secured on the club's assets, its own bank balance and other loans, rather than the equity of the buyer.

In Burnley's case, ALK Capital took out a £65m loan secured against the club's assets, such as Turf Moor , and used £37m from the club's own bank balance.

On top of that, Velocity Capital, the holding company, owed Burnley £80.1m - money which was also used to buy the club.

The original £65m loan was partially paid off, but then refinanced and extended to reach £105m in the 2024-25 accounts. Interest rates were as high as 12%.

On top of that were factored debts, when a club mortgages off future transfer instalments for a one-off payment from the bank. Burnley owed £37m at an interest rate of 12.75%.

In total, the football club's borrowings stood at £142.3m, the 10th-highest external debt in English football.

Then came the 2025-26 accounts, published today, which painted a different picture.

How owners finally paid off £77.7m used to buy Burnley

Now, back to that leveraged buyout which has been attracting so much criticism from fans.

Last season's accounts contained a big surprise.

Remember Velocity Capital, the holding company that owed Burnley £80.1m for the purchase of the club?

The accounts revealed £77.7m of that has now been paid to the Clarets.

It cleared a large chunk of the debt used to buy the football club and helped to make the latest accounts look healthier.

This was needed because, over the past six years, debts related to the leveraged buyout and associated interest payments had increased.

Why Everton's £38.8m compensation was so vital for Burnley

The £77.7m payment, funded by investment from the ownership group, does not mean all Burnley's financial concerns or debts have been resolved.

The club still reported a loss for 2025-26 of £9m, compared with £24m-£29m in the previous three seasons.

But this includes the Velocity Capital payment, money for being in the Premier League - and a landmark compensation payout.

The Clarets have been paid £38.8m by Everton because of the Toffees' profit and sustainability breach in 2021-22, which was found to have impacted Burnley's chances of avoiding relegation that season.

Crucially, however, the payout is subject to an appeal, which is expected to be heard in January.

In the accounts, the board stated that "no provision should be included" for the appeal, the result of which could "range between £Nil and the full value of the award detailed being repayable".

This, the club argues, is because "the outcome of the appeal cannot be reasonably determined or measured".

Without the Everton payment, the loss in the 2025-26 accounts would have been £47.8m rather than £9m - a record loss for the club despite it reporting all-time high revenues of £144.5m for the campaign.

Removing the Everton payment might present a more realistic picture of their finances.

Kieran Maguire, professor of football finance at the University of Liverpool , told BBC Sport that the timing of the accounts is noteworthy, too, coming six months earlier than expected.

"It was a surprise that Burnley filed their accounts now, but it makes sense considering the Everton payment and pending appeal," Maguire said.

"If Everton are successful, and Burnley were to file their accounts next April, the £38.8m could not be included the 2025-26 accounts. So by reporting early, Burnley can include it and avoid potentially recording the record loss."

Premier League football has been seen as key to Burnley's finances - but the accounts show even in the top flight things were a struggle financially.

"The underlying features are that the club was still losing effectively more than £1m a week," Maguire said.

"That was despite the benefits of being in the Premier League, and therefore relying on player sales and the Everton settlement to reduce the figures to something more palatable."

What are the club's current debt levels?

The three influxes of money helped reduce the debt, and heavy interest repayments.

The club's debt now stands at £62.9m, more than half what it was in 2024-25.

But remember, Burnley had been debt free before the takeover.

Bank loans have reduced from £105m to £70.1m.

Burnley had also, in recent seasons, mortgaged off future transfer instalments for a one-off payment from the bank, called 'debt factoring'.

Previously at £37m, they reduced it to £16.1m.

This all looks good, but is still reliant on the payment from Everton . If the Toffees do win their appeal, the picture looks very different.

Added to that, £24.2m of the bank loans is due for repayment in January, with another £21.6m falling next August.

The club is in "negotiations to refinance and increase these facilities", but the accounts note that if an agreement is not reached the owners will require "additional finance to repay the amounts due".

What about next season? It will be a season in the Championship, with much lower revenues and no one-off payment from Everton .

The 2026-27 accounts will include player sales of around £38m and parachute payments of £48m.

On the face of it, the numbers look very encouraging for Burnley.

But the accounts laid out that a number of events, including "the outcome of the ongoing compensation ruling appeal", could continue to "cast significant doubt" on the club as a going concern.

Maguire added: "A more forensic look suggests that the underlying issues at Burnley still exist.

"Given that they were in receipt of Premier League broadcast revenues and the benefits of being in the top division, that does suggest that the club faces ongoing challenges.⁠​⁠‍⁠"

On the field, Burnley need a revival - and fast.

It is still early in the Championship season - 14 games have been played - but Burnley sit in the relegation zone.

Over the past six years, they have been a yo-yo club between the Premier League and the Championship, trading the riches of the top flight with strong revenues from a promotion campaign each season.

A big turnaround is needed for that to still be the case under the new management of Swiss Fabio Celestini , who is yet to win in his two games in charge.

Burnley have recorded just one victory in the opening 14 Championship games, leaving them four points adrift in the bottom three.

Recently they set a new English league record for the longest run without a home win, which will reach 400 days when arch-rivals Blackburn visit Turf Moor on 22 November.

Relegation looks more likely than promotion at the moment, and Burnley cannot afford to become the third team in successive seasons to do the double drop from the Premier League to League One.

But time will tell whether the improved results in the accounts start to be replicated on the pitch.

articles.title: Questions Arise Over the Emergency Treatment Given to Spanish Soccer Player in Fatal Collision
articles.summary: BARCELONA, Spain (AP) — While Spain mourns the death of a soccer player who suffered a cardiac arrest after an on-field collision, the emergency medical treatment he received is falling under scrutiny.
articles.body:
BARCELONA, Spain (AP) — While Spain mourns the death of a soccer player who suffered a cardiac arrest after an on-field collision, the emergency medical treatment he received is falling under scrutiny.

Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel died Tuesday, a day after absorbing a heavy hit by the opposing team's goalkeeper during a match in Spain's second division and being rushed to a hospital.

Spain's National Police opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter — a standard procedure for a non-natural death. Investigators are expected to assess whether Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono's challenge went beyond the normal course of play.

But the incident also raised questions about the on-field treatment the 30-year-old player received after collapsing on the pitch Monday, including how quickly CPR was performed and whether medics used a defibrillator.

Elvira González, the president of Spain's Association of Nurses, Emergency Medics and Caregivers, told The Associated Press on Wednesday that her organization was seeking more information.

"We can't say if they acted correctly or incorrectly, but we can demand that all the emergency procedures follow international standards of correct practice," González said.

Team medical staff was at his side 20 seconds after De Miguel collapsed after being crunched in mid-air by Owono while disputing a high ball late in the game. Emergency workers quickly followed, running a stretcher to the scene in less than a minute.

It is unclear what medical attention De Miguel received during the 5 minutes he was prone on the pitch before being rushed off on a stretcher and placed in an ambulance waiting just off the field.

Some Spanish media reported that he received CPR in the ambulance and recovered a pulse, while others say he received CPR on the field. It has not been established whether a defibrillator was used.

The Tenerife soccer club did not answer repeated calls and an email request asking for more information about the emergency treatment De Miguel received.

"There is contradictory information," González said. "The first thing we need to know is where and when he supposedly recovered a pulse."

She said CPR must be performed from "minute 1" and that using a defibrillator is crucial.

"The first minutes are critical. You can only move a person once a pulse is restored," she said.

On-field treatment proved lifesaving for other athletes who collapsed on the field of play including Danish soccer player Christian Eriksen, whose heart stopped during a European Championship game in 2021. In the NFL, Damar Hamlin of the Buffalo Bills was treated with CPR and defibrillator on the field after he suffered cardiac arrest in 2023. Both survived.

Some local media say that the police probe is also looking into the immediate medical treatment De Miguel received at Tenerife's stadium. The National Police in Madrid and in Tenerife would not comment on that to AP.

Tenerife's largest shareholder Rayco García acknowledged there is still much to be clarified.

"There are those who say that the impact caused his death, and that later they were able to stabilize him artificially even though it was very difficult to bring him back," García told Spanish radio station Cadena Ser on Tuesday. "I prefer to wait for the autopsy and then we can take steps and talk about what needs talking about."

He said the medical team followed protocol and "were fast to get on the field."

But, García added, "I would like to know through the investigation if there is something we don't know so that this doesn't happen again. If there is something that was in our hands to do that could have prevented this tragedy."

When asked why the ambulance didn't enter the field to help evacuate De Miguel, García said the club's medical service didn't order it to approach.

The Spanish soccer federation regulations say that the home team must have at least one doctor on site, and that the home club must have an ambulance equipped with life support, including a defibrillator, at the ready.

La Liga did not respond to request for comment on emergency protocols.

De Miguel's death stunned the soccer community in Spain and beyond. Teams across Europe paid tribute to De Miguel before Champions League games on Tuesday.

Fans left flowers in a makeshift shrine outside Tenerife's stadium.

Owono issued a statement through his club on Wednesday, offering his condolences to De Miguel's family.

"These are the most difficult days of my life," the goalkeeper said. "I feel an immense pain over the loss of Jesús. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him. I know there will be many matters to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect."

De Miguel is survived by his wife and 1-year-old daughter who were at Monday's game. His parents quickly flew to Tenerife, which is part of the Canary Islands archipelago.

The team will travel to the mainland to attend a funeral for De Miguel that García says tentatively will be Thursday in the central province of Toledo.

articles.summary: El máximo accionista del club se está haciendo cargo en primera persona de la crisis emocional que vive la entidad
articles.body: El fútbol español se prepara para darle el último adiós a Jesús de Miguel, futbolista del Tenerife fallecido ayer. Este jueves tendrá lugar el funeral en Navahermosa tras el traslado del cadáver desde la isla hasta el pequeño municipio de su familia en la provincia de Toledo. En el sepelio estará presente Gerard Piqué, que encabezará la expedición del FC Andorra. El máximo accionista del club estará acompañado por Ferran Vilaseca, presidente, y Jaume Nogués, director general y deportivo de la entidad, para presentar sus condolencias y estar junto a la familia de Demi. La plantilla del Andorra, que hoy tuvo un pequeño entrenamiento voluntario, regresará mañana al trabajo, sin Owono, para intentar que el balón cure las heridas y para volver cuanto antes a una normalidad que es casi imposible tras lo vivido el lunes en el Heliodoro Rodríguez López. El fútbol andorrano, a través de su Federación, ha declarado que durante todo el fin de semana se guardará un minuto de silencio en todos los partidos, de todas las categorías, en memoria de Jesús de Miguel. Gerard Piqué se está haciendo cargo en primera persona de la crisis emocional que existe en el club pirenaico. Está en contacto directo con la familia del futbolista y desde el club se estudia hacer en los próximos días unas declaraciones públicas para analizar la situación. Se intenta, además, apartar a Owono, triste protagonista de la jugada que le acabó costando la vida a De Miguel, de todo el ruido mediático en torno a su figura. Quieren que no se sienta culpable y que intente asumir que ha sido un desgraciado accidente. En una carta publicada este miércoles, el portero explica que "están siendo los días más difíciles" de su vida y que le cuesta "encontrar las palabras y asimilar lo que ha pasado". Además, manifiesta que sabe que habrá "muchas cuestiones que abordar" y que afrontará "lo que venga con todo el respeto".

articles.title: Bellingham marca un gol de leyenda para sacar al Madrid de un enredo: "Ha sido instinto"
articles.standfirst: El inglés abrió la remontada en Atenas con un golazo de tacón y se ha consolidado como la pieza clave del Madrid de Mourinho
articles.summary: El inglés abrió la remontada en Atenas con un golazo de tacón y se ha consolidado como la pieza clave del Madrid de Mourinho
articles.body: Hace semanas que es el mejor jugador del Real Madrid. Con goles o sin ellos, pero la versión de Jude Bellingham en esta temporada es de un nivel altísimo. La prolongación de todo lo que se vio en el Mundial y apenas se dejó ver durante la pasada campaña. En la casa del AEK dejó un gol de época, de esos que se recuerdan, de los que se unen para siempre al recuerdo de un partido. De un fuerte pase cruzado de Cucurella sacó un recurso extraordinario para mandar la pelota a las redes de Alberto Brignoli. Un taconazo brillante para alejar la pelota de cualquier intento griego de soñar con evitar el empate. Sometido el Madrid de inicio por el entusiasmo del AEK y por el gran gol de Koita, fue a través de Bellingham por donde el Madrid comenzó a llevar el partido a un terreno más cómodo, más cerca de lo que se esperaba antes de arrancar el encuentro. Su juego, dominante como lo es desde hace semanas, hizo crecer al Madrid. De su genialidad nació un empate que antes se le había escapado al Madrid por un fuera de juego milimétrico. Es el quinto gol de Bellingham en lo que va de temporada, el primero en la Liga de Campeones. En esta competición no marcaba desde la goleada al Mónaco y aquella celebración que dio tanto que hablar. Y es su décima diana en la Champions. Y con el tanto en Atenas, Bellingham se coloca ya como el segundo artillero del Madrid en lo que va de temporada. A la cabeza, lejísimos del resto, aparecen los 15 tantos de Mbappé. El francés tuvo una gran ocasión en el primer tramo del partido, pero su remate se fue a las nubes, lo que provocó una gran frustración en el delantero madridista. Más allá del gol, su plasticidad y su valor, la realidad es que Bellingham se ha convertido en el jugador clave para el funcionamiento del equipo. De su despliegue y llegada nacen muchas de las situaciones de desequilibrio que genera el conjunto de Mourinho. En el haber del técnico portugués está haber recuperado la versión del futbolista que impactó a su llegada a España en el verano de 2023. El propio Bellingham resumió su obra en una idea: “Ha sido instinto. Es un gran centro de Cucurella y le pego de tacón”. El inglés quiso repartir el foco con el héroe del descuento —“Ha sido un gol increíble de Fede contra un rival muy bueno”— y defendió que el triunfo fue merecido: “Creo que hemos sido dominantes durante todo el partido. Han tenido un par de ataques y han marcado, pero hemos tenido el control”. Reivindicó, además, la receta que el Madrid está firmando en Europa: “Hemos trabajado mucho para conseguir esta victoria, hemos tenido el balón y oportunidades, hemos hecho lo que últimamente hacemos en la Champions”. Y puso palabras a su buen momento, el mismo que describe el cuerpo de este texto: “Estoy jugando bien en el centro, teniendo impacto en el partido”.

articles.title: Jesus de Miguel: Canary Islands mourn loss of Tenerife forward
articles.summary: Tenerife football club and the wider football community mourn the loss of footballer Jesus de Miguel following an on-field collision.
articles.body:
As you arrive on the holiday island of Tenerife, there is a profound sense of grief, pain and disbelief at the death of footballer Jesus de Miguel .

The Canary island is in mourning for the Tenerife striker, who died from injuries sustained in a collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a match on Monday.

The 30-year-old had quickly established himself as a club favourite, scoring 11 goals in his first season as Tenerife were promoted to the second tier of Spanish football.

But now the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez Stadium has become a shrine to the player, with hundreds of people gathering throughout the past few days to lay flowers, light candles and pay their respects.

Bouquets, rosettes sent by clubs from across Spain, prayer cards, photographs, children's drawings and scarves have been laid around the grounds outside gate nine.

It is a deeply moving scene. Fans and residents stand in silence, taking in the tributes.

Many are visibly tearful as the scale of the loss begins to sink in at the very place the incident happened.

'Most difficult days of my life' for keeper Owono

Among those paying their respects were Lisa and Lee, visiting Tenerife from Stoke-on-Trent.

They had arrived on holiday at the weekend and decided to attend Monday's match, hoping to experience Spanish football for the first time.

"We never expected something like this to happen," they told BBC Sport.

"We knew it was serious when the players surrounded him [De Miguel], but to see players crying and actually praying on the pitch was very emotional.

"When we found out the news the next day, it just really hit us."

The couple described the atmosphere inside the stadium as sombre and almost completely silent as spectators waited to understand what was happening.

"You always expect somebody to pull through," Lee said. "And then seeing the news the next day, it was just unbelievable."

They returned to the stadium on Wednesday to lay a Port Vale shirt among the tributes, wanting to show their support for the Tenerife community.

"Football has no colours," Lisa said. "If it was one of our players, we'd be heartbroken. They're part of your family."

For Carlos, a player with Tenerife's disability side Tenerife Foundation, the loss is particularly personal.

"Honestly, there are no words to describe him. He was incredible," Carlos said as he lay a flag on the ground.

He described De Miguel as a figure who had helped shape the club's recent history.

"He practically gave his heart and soul for the shirt. He's already a legend at the club because, after all, we were in a very difficult position a few years ago and he helped pull us out of it.

"Without him, I don't think we would be where we are today."

Carlos was at Monday's match and said he was left in shock by what unfolded.

"When I left the stadium I was trembling and I continued to feel that way for hours.

"Right now, we're incredibly hurt and very sad. I also want to send my support to his family, who I can only imagine must be absolutely devastated."

'The club is broken. Absolutely heartbroken'

The sense of loss has extended far beyond the stadium.

Poli Suarez, the Canary Islands' minister for education and sport, said Tenerife was in "complete mourning".

"Canarian sport has been left devastated," Suarez told BBC Sport. "The club is broken. Absolutely heartbroken."

Suarez also stressed that the thoughts of everyone were with De Miguel's wife, daughter and wider family.

"They are the ones suffering most directly from this loss, just as the Tenerife supporters are suffering," he said.

The government has pledged its support to the club, players and supporters, with Suarez describing De Miguel as a footballer who had become part of the Canary Islands' sporting history.

"The loss of Jesus de Miguel is now part of our history," Suarez said.

"Not only because of the circumstances of his death, but also because of the affection he always showed towards our island and towards his club."

A further tribute is planned for Saturday at 18:00 GMT, with supporters encouraged to come together to honour his memory.

"It will be an opportunity to show our affection and emotion, and to demonstrate our solidarity with the family," Suarez said.

"We want to show all our affection for Jesus de Miguel."

articles.title: Joya de la Bundesliga rechaza a Colombia tras la decisión de Néstor Lorenzo
articles.standfirst: Néstor Lorenzo dejó fuera de la Selección Colombia a Santiago Castañeda y eligió jugar con Estados Unidos:
articles.summary: Néstor Lorenzo dejó fuera de la Selección Colombia a Santiago Castañeda y eligió jugar con Estados Unidos:
articles.body: La Selección Colombia tropieza en la gestión de su talento global y deja escapar a una de las promesas con mayor proyección en el fútbol europeo. Ante la falta de llamados formales por parte del cuerpo técnico encabezado por Néstor Lorenzo, el joven mediocampista con presente en la Bundesliga, Santiago Castañeda, tomó una decisión definitiva respecto a su carrera internacional y eligió representar a la Selección de Estados Unidos. La noticia sacude los escritorios de la Federación Colombiana de Fútbol, puesto que el jugador reunía las condiciones y la doble nacionalidad para vestir los colores de la Tricolor, pero la falta de seguimiento y el vacío en las convocatorias inclinaron la balanza de manera irreversible. Santiago Castañeda, volante de 21 años que brilla en el balompié alemán (nacido en Tampa, Estados Unidos, pero con raíces y pasaporte colombiano), venía registrando actuaciones sobresalientes que llamaron la atención de los analistas internacionales. Sin embargo, al no recibir señales concretas ni llamados oficiales por parte de Néstor Lorenzo para integrar el proceso de la Absoluta, el panorama cambió. Pese a haber tenido acercamientos previos y pasos por selecciones juveniles de Estados Unidos, la puerta con Colombia se mantenía teóricamente abierta debido a su ascendencia. No obstante, la inercia en la captación y el llamado de la selección norteamericana terminaron por sellar el destino del mediocampista. Con esta determinación, de acuerdo con el estricto reglamento de elegibilidad de la FIFA, el panorama reglamentario queda zanjado: al consolidar su elección deportiva y sumar minutos oficiales bajo el ala del combinado estadounidense, el volante blinda su elegibilidad, cerrando de forma definitiva cualquier opción de jugar en el futuro para la Selección Colombia. El caso de Santiago Castañeda abre un debate profundo entre los hinchas de la Selección Colombia sobre la eficacia del departamento de scouting y visorías de la FCF en el viejo continente. Mientras las potencias sudamericanas compiten palmo a palmo por asegurar a cada talento con doble nacionalidad que emerge en ligas de Europa, la ausencia de un puente rápido por parte del cuerpo técnico de Néstor Lorenzo vuelve a dejar expuesta a la Tricolor ante la pérdida de futbolistas formados en contextos de alta competencia internacional. Ahora, Estados Unidos celebra la incorporación de una de las joyas más apetecidas del mercado alemán, mientras que en Colombia queda el sinsabor de una oportunidad desaprovechada en el relevo generacional.

articles.title: Hearts lose Calvin Miller for two months as injuries mount
articles.summary: Heart of Midlothian will be without Calvin Miller for two months after the winger suffered a knee injury that requires surgery in Sunday's Premier Sports Cup semi-final defeat by Hibernian.
articles.body:
Heart of Midlothian will be without Calvin Miller for two months after the winger suffered a knee injury that requires surgery in Sunday's Premier Sports Cup semi-final defeat by Hibernian.

Thomas Magnusson will also be out until after the international break after the midfielder suffered concussion in the first half at Hampden Park.

It adds to Hearts' already lengthy injury list that means head coach Wouter Vrancken will take only 19 players - six short of the normal maximum squad size of 25 - to Switzerland for Thursday's Conference League match against Thun.

The absence of Miller and Magnusson means the Edinburgh side now have 10 first-team players sidelined through injury.

Hearts took an early lead at Hampden, but Magnusson was then forced off after only 14 minutes.

Miller, who had set up Claudio Braga's opener, himself followed to the dressing room on 37 minutes, with Hibs taking a 2-1 lead shortly after.

Until his injury, the uncapped 28-year-old was being touted by some as a possible inclusion in the latest Scotland squad announced by Vrancken's fellow Belgian, Sebastien Pocognoli, after fellow winger Josh McPake and striker James Wilson were called up last month.
