articles.title: Scotland U21 boss hails Donovan, Miller and Wilson attitude
articles.summary: Under-21s head coach Tony Docherty is delighted with the buy-in from the three players who have dropped down from Scotland's senior squad.
articles.body:
Under-21s head coach Tony Docherty is delighted with the buy-in from the three players who have dropped down from Scotland's senior squad.

Celtic right-back Colby Donovan, Udinese midfielder Lennon Miller and Heart of Midlothian striker James Wilson have all been included in a new-look Scotland Under-21 squad for friendlies against Ukraine and United States in Spain this month.

The three players were all in Sebastian Pocogonoli's first full Scotland squad and join Manchester United midfielder Tyler Fletcher, who went to the World Cup before joining Docherty's group in September.

"I'm really, really delighted with the introduction of the ones that have had that A squad experience and they're really the drivers," Docherty said.

Upward path for Penrice has McInnes eager for Rangers deal

Welsh injury adds to Swans' misery at Portsmouth

Pocognoli focus on Scotland tidy-up as Euros loom

"They become your leadership group that drives standards, create that mentality, get that identity.

"You've seen that in the last camp when I was out at the A squad camp and I returned with James and Findlay [Curtis] and then Findlay goes back up again as a result of his performance.

"Lennon and Colby Donovan, I've had dialogue with both of them quite a bit over the last couple of days, just to outline what their pathway is.

"If they're not going to be getting minutes for this camp with the A squad, it's important they come in to my squad and it will be a mirror image in terms of structure, fundamentals. And they just come in and get an opportunity to get game time."

Miller had hoped that last summer's transfer from Motherwell to Udinese would cement his place in the senior squad, but the 20-year-old finds himself in the area of the pitch with most strength in depth.

"I had a particularly long conversation with Lennon," Docherty revealed. "You've seen the example, the last camp there with Barney Stewart. He comes in, he scores three goals, he's in a good place when he gets back, gets into West Brom's first team, scores a couple of goals, they win a couple of games.

"I had a good conversation with Colby and he just wants to play. So it's important that we've got the buy-in. It's not us telling Colby, 'you're playing with the 21s', it's him in dialogue with us saying, 'I want to do that, I want to play and I want to impress'."

Meanwhile, St Mirren striker Eseosa Sule has been called up as Docherty prepares for a new European qualifying campaign after 16 of the 27 players from his first squad went beyond the age level.

Rangers youth forward Kyle Glasgow drops to the Scotland Under-19 squad for three European qualifying games.

The 16-year-old currently on loan to Alloa Athletic joins elder brother Euan Glasgow, who plays for Edinburgh City on loan from Hearts.

Goalkeepers: Sam Kane (Derby County), Rory Mahady (Leeds United), Aidan Rice (Dumbarton on loan from Celtic).

Defenders: Daniel Armer (Manchester United), Murray Campbell (Burnley), Colby Donovan (Celtic), Josh Dede (Middlesbrough), Mitchel Frame (Aberdeen), Dylan Smith (Ross County), Ethan Sutherland (Exeter City on loan from Wolverhampton Wanderers), John Tod (Dunfermline Athletic).

Midfielders: Calum Adamson (Raith Rovers on loan from Rangers), Aidan Borland (Accrington Stanley on loan from Aston Villa), Tyler Fletcher (Manchester United), Lennon Miller (Udinese), Calum McLeod (Inverness Caledonian Thistle), Kyle Ure (Crewe Alexandra on loan from Celtic), Dylan Watret (Ayr United).

Forwards: Findlay Marshall (Aberdeen), Alfie Stewart (Inverness Caledonian Thistle on loan from Aberdeen), Eseosa Sule (St Mirren), Andrew Tod (Dunfermline Athletic), James Wilson (Heart of Midlothian).

articles.title: Karetsas "very happy" with maiden BVB goal, Anton hails team enthusiasm
articles.summary: Kostas Karetsas was Borussia Dortmund's hero on the night as his goal ensured a 2-1 victory against Real Betis at the Westfalenstadion.I’m obviously very hap...
articles.body:
Kostas Karetsas was Borussia Dortmund's hero on the night as his goal ensured a 2-1 victory against Real Betis at the Westfalenstadion.

I'm obviously very happy. It hasn't always been easy for me recently," Karetsas said after the game, referencing his spell of injury setbacks.

"That's why I'm really glad I came on today and was able to make a real contribution to the team [by scoring a goal].

"I think we put in a very good performance and deserved to win. Betis have a very strong team," the Greek talent said of their Spanish visitors.

Another key man at the heart of BVB's defence was Waldemar Anton. He expressed his joy at taking another big Champions League step.

"We took control of the key phases of the match today and made further progress," the defender said in the mixed zone at full-time.

"That was a very important win today at this stage of the season, but we still have a long way to go [to qualify for the knockouts].

"We're in good form and everyone in the team is keen to give it their all – including the players who come on as substitutes," he concluded.

The North-Rhine Westphalian giants next port of call returns them to Bundesliga action, taking on SV Elversberg this Saturday at 15:30 CET.

articles.title: 51 red cards shown in Brazilian youth game between Uberlandia and Mamore
articles.summary: A world record of 43 players and eight members of staff were sent off during an under-20 championship match between Uberlandia and Mamore in Brazil.
articles.body:
A world record of 51 red cards were shown during a chaotic under-20s game in Brazil.

The semi-final first leg of the Minas Gerais Under-20 Championship tie between Uberlandia and Mamore was marred by scenes that led to 43 players and eight members of coaching staff being sent off.

The previous record was 36, in a 2011 fifth-division game between Club Atletico Claypole and Victoriano Arenas in Argentina.

Brazilian news outlet O Tempo reported the military police were called , external because of extensive damage to the Parque do Sabia Stadium.

According to the referee's report, a brawl broke out in the second half after Mamores' Davi taunted the opposition bench during celebrations when his side went 3-1 up.

Uberlandia goalkeeping coach Paulo Sergio Dias Dos Santos ran on to the pitch to confront him, sparking clashes and the subsequent dismissals, with three players having already been sent off earlier.

The police report referenced 14 broken doors, damaged shower facilities, broken windows and that benches, tables and chairs had been destroyed.

The game was paused for approximately 40 minutes and then abandoned by referee Fernando Patrick Drosghic Modesto.

Uberlandia have since confirmed , external that they have conceded the second leg of the semi-final because Mamore only have seven players available as a result of all the red cards.

They described their move as a "gesture of fair play" as Mamore would progress through to the final, and Uberlandia will instead focus on the third-place match.

articles.title: La parada imposible de Álvaro Valles
articles.standfirst: El rinconero pudo hacer más en el 2-1, pero salvó al Betis en muchas otras ocasiones
articles.summary: El rinconero pudo hacer más en el 2-1, pero salvó al Betis en muchas otras ocasiones
articles.body: Álvaro Valles pudo hacer algo más en el segundo tanto del Borussia Dortmund en el cuarto partido de la fase de liguilla de la Champions League, pero se lució con intervenciones geniales en el Signal Iduna Park. El guardameta del Betis está en la prelista de Luis de la Fuente de cara a los compromisos que la Selección atenderá en el próximo parón internacional. En el minuto 20 llegó una de las paradas de esta jornada de Champions. Ryerson llegó cerca de la línea de fondo y metió el pase para Svensson, que remató a menos de dos metros de la portería, pero Valles se tiró con todo y la taponó. Ya en la segunda mitad sacó una mano baja a Karetsas y a veinte minutos del final detuvo un cabezazo de Jobe Bellingham. Siempre mantuvo vivo a su equipo. "Son un gran equipo, jugaban en su campo y presionaban muy bien la salida de balón y nos obligaba a jugar más directo. Lo hemos hecho bastante bien. En la segunda parte hemos encontrado más espacio y hemos apretado, pero no hemos tenido la fortuna de empatar. Nos vamos con un sabor amargo", comentó el rinconero tras el partido. El Betis dio la cara ante un grande. "Nos vamos con una gran sensación de competirle a un gran equipo. Le hemos plantado cara y hemos estado cerca de rascar puntos, con el convencimiento de que el trabajo está y el equipo ha hecho todo lo posible. Este es el camino", finalizó.
